Event: `2bf84be0716979a77c694694e8fd1dfd` · 2026-09-26T00:38:45Z

> Verdict: MERGE (notes only). Checked: kernel boot_log_endpoint (budget.rs) gives the receive right only to the bundle's first program, badge 0, installed last; sends in slot 2 badged with the kernel-assigned PID. console::relay prefixes every split line with [pid N]/[badge N] and maps control chars (incl. CR) to '?', so no relayed text can start a line with '[server] done:'. The testbench anchors DONE_LINE, forbids any DONE that is not the reporter's or a second one, and fails poweroff without it. DONE's PID comes from m.badge (kernel-written). TAKE_GIFTS gives budgets only (never devices, R2), once; log-server closes its copies. UPPERCASE writes into a lend, which the spec guarantees writable (KERNEL-SPEC 166), so a client cannot crash the server with a read-only lend. Received handles are closed at once, so the table cannot be filled.
> 
> P3-1 logsrv.rs Line::Done/GiftsGiven print m.badge as 'pid N'. A minted child badge (>=0x100) would read 'reported by pid 256'. The bench regex needs pid<=64 so nothing breaks, but the label lies. Suggest printing through the same pid/badge rule as relay.
> P3-2 TAKE_GIFTS goes to the first caller, whoever that is. A sibling that runs before the attacker gets root/system/users. In today's cases the attacker then fails loudly on Refused (no silent pass), and the fixture is INTERIM until R3. Worth one sentence in docs/testbench.md rule F.
> P3-3 The legacy server (serve_legacy) still relays with pid 0 when sender.pid() is None. That is expected, since legacy is deleted in a later commit. Confirm its deletion closes this in the next round.
> Not done this round: plant-and-revert experiments. Nothing in 1-2 deletes an attack case; logsrv-badge-forgery and bench-reporter-mismatch are new bites, and I'll plant them when the legacy decoder is removed.
